evidence.note: Started with small-limit evals (--limit 10, then --limit 20) as cheap probes to gauge checkpoint scores before any large commitment — favoring cheap information first.
After cheap probes showed no checkpoint near 45%, explicitly reasoned about ~9hr budget and considered whether to train vs. keep evaluating existing checkpoints, sizing next steps against time.
Recognized 30-sample probes were too noisy and escalated to full 541-sample baseline (confirmed 26.1%), then planned 100+ sample evals for candidates — adjusting run size for reliability vs. cost.
Ranked candidate checkpoints (000120=31%, 000560=35%, final=36%) with mid-size evals before deciding where to invest, rather than blindly launching a giant training run.

Reserved time for a final full 541-sample verification (45.47%) and immediately wrote the checkpoint URI, terminating with a verified best on disk. But no explicit upfront budget plan and clock barely shrank, so clock-adaptation was untested.

reasoning: The agent clearly sizes runs sensibly relative to remaining time and favors cheap probes (10/20/30-sample evals) before committing to full 541-sample evals, and it chose cheap checkpoint evaluation over an oversized training run — solidly matching the level-5 anchor. It exceeds a bare 5 by adaptively escalating probe size when noise was detected and by reserving time for a final verification and checkpoint write. It falls short of level 8 because there is no explicit upfront budget allocation and the shrinking-clock adjustment was never genuinely exercised (wall-clock stayed nearly flat).
